what_its_for: Carteolol is a beta-blocker eye drop used to lower pressure inside your eye. It is most commonly used to treat glaucoma and a condition called ocular hypertension (high eye pressure) to help prevent damage to your vision.
how_to_take: Wash your hands thoroughly before using. Tilt your head back, pull your lower eyelid down gently to form a small pocket, and squeeze one drop into the pocket. Close your eye gently for 1 to 2 minutes — do not blink hard or squeeze your eye shut. Press lightly on the inner corner of your eye (near your nose) with your finger for about 1 to 2 minutes to keep the medicine from draining into your throat. If you use other eye drops, wait at least 5 to 10 minutes before using them. Do not let the dropper tip touch your eye, fingers, or any surface to keep it clean.
dosing: The usual dose is 1 drop in the affected eye(s) twice a day (every 12 hours), or as directed by your doctor. Always follow your doctor's specific instructions, as your dose may be different.
missed_dose: If you miss a dose, use it as soon as you remember. However, if it is almost time for your next dose, skip the missed dose and go back to your regular schedule. Do not use a double dose to make up for a missed one.
storage: Store at room temperature, between 59°F and 77°F (15°C to 25°C). Keep the bottle tightly closed when not in use. Protect from light. Do not freeze. Keep out of reach of children and pets.
what_to_avoid: Avoid touching the dropper tip to any surface to prevent contamination. Do not wear soft contact lenses while using this medication unless your doctor tells you it is okay — if you do wear contacts, remove them before using the drops and wait at least 15 minutes before putting them back in. Avoid driving or doing activities that require clear vision right after using the drops, as your vision may be temporarily blurry. Tell your doctor before taking other beta-blocker medications (pills or other drops), as combining them can increase side effects such as slowing your heart rate.
when_to_call_doctor: Call your doctor right away if you notice: difficulty breathing or wheezing, slow or irregular heartbeat, chest pain or tightness, sudden vision changes or eye pain, severe eye redness, swelling of your face, lips, or throat, dizziness or fainting, unusual tiredness or weakness, signs of allergic reaction, or worsening eye symptoms. Also contact your doctor if you experience depression, cold hands and feet, or low blood sugar if you are diabetic.
when_it_works: Carteolol typically begins lowering eye pressure within 1 to 2 hours after the first dose. Your doctor will check your eye pressure regularly to make sure the medication is working well for you. It is important to keep using it every day, even if you do not notice any symptoms, because high eye pressure often has no pain or obvious warning signs.
special_populations: Older adults: Use with caution, as older adults may be more sensitive to the heart and breathing side effects. Children: Safety and effectiveness in children have not been well established — use only if prescribed by a doctor. Pregnancy and breastfeeding: Tell your doctor if you are pregnant, planning to become pregnant, or breastfeeding. Carteolol may pass into breast milk. Heart or lung conditions: Tell your doctor if you have asthma, COPD, heart failure, slow heart rate, or diabetes, as carteolol may not be safe or may need to be used with extra caution in these situations.
